newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity sees modest growth this year.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity sees modest growth this year.

text.p: Anglo-U.S. engineering group LucasVarity Plc said on Thursday that despite adverse currency movements in the first quarter, it was on "track to deliver modest, top-line growth" this year.

The company also unveiled that first quarter pre-tax profits had risen 16 percent to 72 million pounds ($117.6 million)against 62 million last time, based on proforma combined results following the merger between Lucas Industries and Varity Corp in September 1996.
LucasVarity said that it expects automotive markets in both Europe and North America to be relatively flat for the remainder of this year.
"Within Europe, the Italian, Spanish and UK markets are expected to out-perform last year, whilst the French market continues to be weak," said chief executive Victor Rice in a statement.
He described the first quarter performance as "creditable start to the year" against a background of mixed trading conditions and the strength of sterling.

Sales in the first quarter rose 8.6 percent to 1.21 billion pounds despite the strength of the pound having a translation depreciation on sales of around 50 million pounds during this period, said the company.
